queue.why: The warmth half of the owner's complaint has a single upstream cause and it is not the objects. Measured this firing: every paper stock carries 3-5x more chroma in its dusk render than in its day render, off the same albedo and the same recipe -- lined_01 is Cmean 0.0132 by day and 0.0554 at dusk. That is not exposure. Darkening the day render by the same three stops the dusk rig stops down measures 0.0067, which is 0.51x, because OKLab chroma scales as the cube root of a uniform exposure change: exposure moves chroma the WRONG way, so the illuminant's hue is doing all of the work and more. The day rig's net illuminant is a near-white sun (1.0, 0.965, 0.905) at 2.6 plus a COOL sky fill (0.80, 0.83, 0.87) at 0.55, which comes to R:G:B = 1.000:0.975:0.931 -- essentially neutral. The build is not desaturated because its objects are grey. It is desaturated because it is lit by a neutral lamp, and objects rendered under that lamp can never be more chromatic than their own albedo.

queue.note: Proved by render, not by argument. blender/paper/stocks.py was run twice at res 700 / samples 10 / --condition day on `lined` variant 1, once against the committed blender/rig/common.py and once against a copy with DAY_SKY moved from (0.80, 0.83, 0.87) to (0.92, 0.84, 0.70), everything else identical. Result: ground mean_chroma 0.0142 -> 0.0278, which is +96% and almost the whole way to the 0.030 floor from a single constant; ground p99_chroma 0.0273 -> 0.0366 against a ceiling of 0.09, so the ceiling is not remotely threatened; lightness L50 0.9675 -> 0.9699, i.e. the sheet gets very slightly LIGHTER, not darker; and contrast against the three body inks IMPROVES -- ballpoint 12.98 -> 13.06, graphite 10.33 -> 10.40, margin 8.57 -> 8.63. Warmth here is free of legibility cost, which is the opposite of what one would assume and is why it is written down. Read the ratios, not the absolutes: this render is res 700 / samples 10 / PNG and the shipped asset is res 3000 / samples 24 / WebP, so its L50 is 0.9675 where the committed lined_01.webp is 0.9306. The comparison is baseline-vs-warmed under identical settings and is valid; the absolute numbers do not transfer. (0.92, 0.84, 0.70) is a probe, not a proposal -- a tint sweep over the committed asset puts the net illuminant needed to clear the ground floor at about B=0.80. DESIGN should pick the actual value, because the day illuminant is DIRECTION.md's light section and not an implementation detail, and because it moves every asset in the build at once. This supersedes the conclusion recorded at firing 3 that the charm floors need 26 new object renders: they need one light.

routine.name: love-tap improvement loop
routine.delivery: self-bound: the Routine wakes the session that created it, and that session spawns a fresh repository-attached worker per firing with create_session
designs_that_do_not_work: Routine mints a fresh session which pushes: a minted session gets sources: [] and the proxy injects no push credential, so git push is a deterministic 403.

The minted session attaches the repository itself: it has no MCP tools. One probe told to call add_repo then push landed nothing; another told to call create_session produced no session and returned in eight seconds.

Routine wakes a named persistent orchestrator: its container had been reclaimed and the wake never re-provisioned it. Fired 22:20; the session's updated_at never moved and the Routine recorded no last_run at all.
traps_paid_for_already: list_triggers reports last_run SUCCEEDED for a firing that achieved nothing: it records delivery, not accomplishment. A commit on origin is the only proof.

update_trigger has no persistent_session_id parameter -- only create_trigger does. Passing it to update_trigger is silently ignored, so a rebinding needs the Routine recreated. Read persist_session back rather than trusting the call.
create_session cannot make a child more permissive than its parent, so a dispatcher must be created from a session that is not in plan mode or it inherits plan and stalls for ever.
routine.when_it_stops: The dispatcher is a real session with a real context window. If it fills or is archived the loop stops silently and the branch simply stops gaining commits. The fix is to create the Routine again from a new session, which is two calls; nothing is lost because loop/STATE.json holds the state.
